doc:
Item 2: typed-input mutual-derivation result (Rust-owned).

When the user types into one of the limit double-layout inputs (price /
quantity / amount), Native dispatches the matching action and the Manager
recomputes the dependent field. Native echoes the recomputed string back
into the *other* input (controlled-input SRP) and never performs the
`price × qty` / `amount ÷ price` math itself (A1/A2 compliance) — exactly
the seekbar `CTSpotSeekbarState` contract.

`target` names which input the recomputed `value` should be written to:
`"amount"` (price/qty change → recompute quote amount) or `"quantity"`
(amount change → recompute base qty). `value` is `""` when an input was
cleared / invalid (Native clears the dependent field). `version` is a
monotonic counter so an identical recompute still re-renders.

doc:
UI-ready slim VO for the option position close-all entry points.

Replaces the legacy `TradePositionManager.PositionItem` previously rebuilt
(via `PurePositionRawInfoMapper.toPositionItem`) at the two option-close
`toPositionItem` sites in `PurePositionListFragment`:

1. `handleOptionClose` → `CloseOptionFragment.newInstance(positionItem)`
(the native V1 limit-close order panel — reads `instId` / `instType` /
`availPos` and runs its own biz lookups + `TradePresenter.makeOrderRequest`
internally; it is NOT a Pure fragment, so only the three fields it reads

2. `optionPositionCloseRedirect` → `PureOptionPositionCloseAllBottomSheet`
(the block-trade RFQ shell, driven by the Rust `OptionPositionCloseInteractor`).

The RFQ shell previously read off `PositionItem`:
- **interactor init params** — `instId`, `pos.abs → sz`, `getMarginModel()
→ td_mode`, `getSide() → quote_side` (`startInteractor`,
`PureOptionPositionCloseAllBottomSheet.kt:148-168`). All UI-ready here.
- **`initPositionInfo`** (`...:253-272`) — `TradeTitleUtils.changeTitle
(getSuggestedInstrument)` → `title_parts` (via `CTPositionFormatter::
format_title`), `getCoinUrl(tradeSymbol)` → `coin_url`, `getPositionsSide()`
→ `position_side` (the 4-way side used for the buy/sell tag; Native maps
`net_buy`/`net_sell` to the buy/sell tag CDKey + OKDS style).

The per-quote price / amount / estimated-PnL row depends on the runtime
best-quote price (only known once `OptionPositionCloseInteractor` emits
`QuoteReceived`), so it is NOT on this VO — it is produced on demand by
`get_option_close_quote(pos_id, quote_px)` → [`OktOptionCloseQuoteVo`].

doc:
V1 `OptionLimitTradePanelPresenter.checkInputFocus` (`:362`, base
`OptionTradePanelPresenter:470`). Pre-submit focus gate — decides which input
(if any) to focus before pre-check, in the SAME order as native:
- price empty / numerically zero → `Price`. Native `price.isNullOrEmpty() ||
price.eq("0")`; price is never negative (numeric input), so empty-or-non-
positive is equivalent to empty-or-zero.
- amount empty / `<= 0`, and the percent seekbar is NOT driving the amount →
`Probably`. Native `contract.lte("0") && isSeekBarSelectedPercent() != true`;

fields.name: trade_with_balances
fields.doc:
Per-ccy DISPLAY-READY available balance for the Trade-With picker rows,
keyed by quote ccy. Twin of `AssetTpslState::trade_quote_ccy_balances`,
built by the same shared `usd_settle_ccy_manager::build_balance_display`
(a `TradingNumber` amount truncated DOWN to the coin `sizeDig` + the
`BALANCE_KEY` label + the ccy unit), so both sheets render byte-identical
balance lines. Native resolves the `DisplayString` directly — NO Kotlin
re-formatting (the legacy `formatTradeWithBalanceLabel` convertor path is
not used by the Rust sheet).

Sourced from a ONE-SHOT HTTP GET of
`/priapi/v5/account/balance?ccy=<picker ccys>` (NOT a WS subscription),
login-gated. A key missing from this map is the pre-network state and
renders as the "--" placeholder; a ccy the backend omits comes back as
"0" (native parity — `fetchTradeWithBalances` fills "0", not "--").

Deliberately a TOP-LEVEL state field, NOT a member of
[`OktHeaderTradeWithVo`]: `HeaderManager` rebuilds the whole `trade_with`
VO on every snapshot tick, so a field living inside it would be wiped by
the next unrelated data update — exactly the bug `mmr_state` /
`mmr_display` already carry a warning for in `HeaderInteractor`. Sole
writer: the `TradeWithBalances` coordinator.
